title: Support aliases for subcommands registered on a click.Group
instruction:
# Support aliases for subcommands of a `click.Group`

Add short alternative names for subcommands, for example `ls` for `list`.

## API

- `click.Command(..., aliases=None)`: a new keyword argument accepting a sequence of
  strings. It is stored as a tuple on `Command.aliases` (an empty tuple when not given).
  Because the `@command` / `@group.command()` decorators forward extra keyword arguments,
  `@cli.command("list", aliases=["ls"])` must work, and so must groups created with
  `aliases=`.

## Group behaviour

1. Registration: aliases are registered when a command is added with
   `Group.add_command` and also for commands passed to `Group(commands=...)`
   (as a mapping or a sequence).
2. Resolution: `Group.get_command(ctx, name)` returns the command for a registered alias.
   Invoking a group with an alias runs that command exactly as its canonical name would,
   including in `chain=True` groups.
3. The canonical name is reported everywhere: `ctx.invoked_subcommand` of the group and
   `info_name` of the subcommand's context are the name the command is registered under,
   not the alias.
4. `list_commands` does not include aliases. Unknown names still produce the existing
   `No such command '…'.` error.
5. Help: in the group's `Commands` section, a command with aliases is listed as
   `name (alias1, alias2)` (aliases in declaration order, separated by `", "`).
   Commands without aliases are listed exactly as before.
6. Conflicts raise `ValueError` at registration time:
   - an alias equal to another registered command's name:
     `Alias {alias!r} of command {name!r} is already a command name.`
   - an alias already used by another command:
     `Alias {alias!r} of command {name!r} is already an alias of command {other!r}.`
   - registering a command whose name is an existing alias of a different command:
     `Command name {name!r} is already an alias of command {other!r}.`
7. Re-registering a command under the same name replaces it, and the aliases of the
   replaced command are dropped (only the new command's aliases remain registered).

`Command.to_info_dict()` must not change. All existing behaviour and the existing test
suite must keep working.
solution_patch:
diff --git a/src/click/core.py b/src/click/core.py
index e4b6b57..1ebeffa 100644
--- a/src/click/core.py
+++ b/src/click/core.py
@@ -984,6 +984,12 @@ class Command:
                         indicating that the command is deprecated and highlights
                         its deprecation in --help. The message can be customized
                         by using a string as the value.
+    :param aliases: Alternative names a :class:`Group` also accepts for this
+        command. They are listed next to the command's name in the group's
+        help page.
+
+    .. versionchanged:: 8.6
+        Added the ``aliases`` parameter.
 
     .. versionchanged:: 8.2
         This is the base class for all commands, not ``BaseCommand``.
@@ -1032,6 +1038,7 @@ class Command:
     no_args_is_help: bool
     hidden: bool
     deprecated: bool | str
+    aliases: tuple[str, ...]
 
     def __init__(
         self,
@@ -1047,6 +1054,7 @@ class Command:
         no_args_is_help: bool = False,
         hidden: bool = False,
         deprecated: bool | str = False,
+        aliases: cabc.Sequence[str] | None = None,
     ) -> None:
         #: the name the command thinks it has.  Upon registering a command
         #: on a :class:`Group` the group will default the command name
@@ -1076,6 +1084,8 @@ class Command:
         self.no_args_is_help = no_args_is_help
         self.hidden = hidden
         self.deprecated = deprecated
+        #: Alternative names a group resolves to this command.
+        self.aliases = tuple(aliases or ())
 
     def to_info_dict(self, ctx: Context) -> dict[str, t.Any]:
         return {
@@ -1749,6 +1759,11 @@ class Group(Command):
 
         #: The registered subcommands by their exported names.
         self.commands = commands
+        #: Maps each registered alias to the name of its command.
+        self._aliases: dict[str, str] = {}
+
+        for name, command in commands.items():
+            self._register_aliases(name, command)
 
         if no_args_is_help is None:
             no_args_is_help = not invoke_without_command
@@ -1808,8 +1823,46 @@ class Group(Command):
         if name is None:
             raise TypeError("Command has no name.")
         _check_nested_chain(self, name, cmd, register=True)
+
+        owner = self._aliases.get(name)
+
+        if owner is not None and owner != name:
+            raise ValueError(
+                f"Command name {name!r} is already an alias of command {owner!r}."
+            )
+
+        self._register_aliases(name, cmd)
         self.commands[name] = cmd
 
+    def _register_aliases(self, name: str, cmd: Command) -> None:
+        """Register the aliases of ``cmd``, registered under ``name``.
+
+        Replacing a command drops the aliases of the command it replaces.
+        """
+        aliases = getattr(cmd, "aliases", ())
+
+        for alias in aliases:
+            if alias != name and alias in self.commands:
+                raise ValueError(
+                    f"Alias {alias!r} of command {name!r} is already a command name."
+                )
+
+            owner = self._aliases.get(alias)
+
+            if owner is not None and owner != name:
+                raise ValueError(
+                    f"Alias {alias!r} of command {name!r} is already an alias of"
+                    f" command {owner!r}."
+                )
+
+        self._aliases = {
+            alias: owner for alias, owner in self._aliases.items() if owner != name
+        }
+
+        for alias in aliases:
+            if alias != name:
+                self._aliases[alias] = name
+
     @t.overload
     def command(self, __func: t.Callable[..., t.Any]) -> Command: ...
 
@@ -1959,8 +2012,17 @@ class Group(Command):
     def get_command(self, ctx: Context, cmd_name: str) -> Command | None:
         """Given a context and a command name, this returns a :class:`Command`
         object if it exists or returns ``None``.
+
+        .. versionchanged:: 8.6
+            Also resolves command aliases.
         """
-        return self.commands.get(cmd_name)
+        cmd = self.commands.get(cmd_name)
+        owner = getattr(self, "_aliases", {}).get(cmd_name)
+
+        if cmd is None and owner is not None:
+            cmd = self.commands.get(owner)
+
+        return cmd
 
     def list_commands(self, ctx: Context) -> list[str]:
         """Returns a list of subcommand names in the order they should appear."""
@@ -1988,6 +2050,11 @@ class Group(Command):
             if cmd.hidden:
                 continue
 
+            aliases = getattr(cmd, "aliases", ())
+
+            if aliases:
+                subcommand = f"{subcommand} ({', '.join(aliases)})"
+
             commands.append((subcommand, cmd))
 
         # allow for 3 times the default spacing
@@ -2109,6 +2176,11 @@ class Group(Command):
             if _split_opt(cmd_name)[0]:
                 self.parse_args(ctx, args)
             raise NoSuchCommand(cmd_name, possibilities=self.commands, ctx=ctx)
+
+        # An alias resolves to the name its command is registered under.
+        if cmd is not None and cmd_name not in self.commands:
+            cmd_name = getattr(self, "_aliases", {}).get(cmd_name, cmd_name)
+
         return cmd_name if cmd else None, cmd, args[1:]
 
     def shell_complete(self, ctx: Context, incomplete: str) -> list[CompletionItem]:
